title: Model deploy pipeline sync — decision journal (mlops integration)
content:
Meeting: Model deploy pipeline sync — platform + applied-ml + serving-runtime
Date: 2026-03-10
Location: Zoom / #platform-engineering
Attendees: Aisha Gupta (owner), Marco Alvarez (serving-runtime), Jing Wei (applied-ml), Samir Patel (security), Lena Rossi (release-eng), Oliver Park (sre), + notes from Eric (product via chat)
Purpose: Walk through proposed MLOps integration RFC for model artifacts, canary rollout policy, and automated rollback/telemetry gating. Capture final decisions, open tradeoffs, and concrete next actions for implementation across Platform, Serving Runtime, and Security.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Agreed on a two-stage deploy pipeline for hosted/dedicated/private that centralizes artifact signing + provenance before artifact promotion to staging.
- Canary rollout window will be metric-driven (latency + quality) with a 10–15 minute minimum observation period and guardrails for token-cost regression.
- Automated rollback will be enforced via a consensus of observability signals (model-quality regression OR 2x latency spike OR elevated error rate) — rollback will happen automatically for Hosted, and be configurable/autonomous for Dedicated/Private.
- Owned implementation tasks assigned; plan to start prototyping in serving-runtime feature branch next sprint.

Context and constraints discussed
- Business need: Reduce production regressions from model updates; speed up safe promotion for teams using Hosted API while giving Dedicated/Private customers control.
- Constraints: Diverse deploy targets (hosted vs. private), strict audit/KMS requirements for enterprise customers, and limited observability coverage for certain private on-prem networks.
- Non-goal: Full integration with customer CI (out-of-scope for initial rollout).

Decisions (finalized during session)
1) Artifact provenance & signing: All models entering the deployment pipeline must carry a signed artifact bundle (model weights + manifest + eval snapshot). Signature mode: HSM-backed signatures via KMS integration. For Hosted, Redwood signs end-to-end; for Dedicated/Private, we support either Redwood-sign or customer-provided signatures (BYO) depending on contract. Rationale: auditability + preventing tampered binaries.

2) Promotion flow (two-stage):
   - Stage 1 (Validation/Staging): artifact accepted -> automated eval suite runs (unit prompts + benchmark prompts from applied-ml) -> lightweight contract tests (shape, kv-cache sanity, latency smoke).
   - Stage 2 (Canary -> Gradual): small percentage traffic to canary variant with continuous eval hooks. Canary progresses automatically based on pass criteria OR holds for manual review. Rationale: quick feedback loop while limiting blast radius.

3) Canary gating criteria (numeric thresholds set here as defaults; teams can override with justifications):
   - Latency: p95 increase <= 20% relative to baseline and absolute p95 < 350ms for hosted-api models under typical request sizes.
   - Error rate: request error rate <= baseline + 0.1% absolute.
   - Model quality: prompt-sets (n=250) pass >= 98% of prior model's quality checks (applied-ml metric: normalized semantic-similarity + hallucination filter).
   - Token cost delta: per-token compute cost increase <= 10% unless flagged by product.

4) Automated rollback policy: For Hosted deployments, if any critical guardrail fails (quality drop > 3% absolute OR sustained p95 > 2x baseline for 5 minutes OR error rate > baseline + 0.5%) then rollback triggers automatically + incident created. For Dedicated/Private, default is automated rollback disabled; platform API exposes opt-in toggle with recommended defaults for customers. Rationale: Hosted needs stronger SLA; enterprise customers want control.

5) Observability signals & ownership: Serving-runtime will emit a standardized telemetry envelope: request-id, model-variant-id, latency buckets, token-usage, feature-flag-state, and evaluation-snapshot ID. Platform-engineering owns the alerting runbooks and promotion orchestration; SRE will own incident runbooks.

6) Contract tests for runtime compatibility: A compact test matrix (ABI checks, KV cache behavior, quantization compatibility) will be executed in the staging-environment. Failing tests block promotion.

Alternatives considered and tradeoffs
- Signed manifests v.s. content-addressed artifacts: Content-addressing (e.g., by SHA) is more rigorous but requires a broad change to artifact storage and caching. We agreed to sign bundles now and evaluate moving to content-addressable storage in Q3.
- Manual-only canary v.s. automated gating: Manual reduces false positives but slows velocity. The mixed approach (automatic with hard fail gates + manual hold option) gives a balance.
- Always-enable automated rollback v.s. opt-in for enterprise: Enterprise customers often have policies requiring manual approvals; opt-in avoids surprises.

Open questions (need follow-up)
- How do we collect ground-truth quality labels quickly for canaries where behavior change is semantic? Jing to prototype a miniature human-in-the-loop micro-eval harness for critical routes (due 2026-03-24).
- For on-prem Private deployments with limited telemetry, what minimal signals are necessary? Samir and Oliver to draft a minimal telemetry contract (peer review 2026-03-17).
- Should we store per-candidate eval snapshots for 90 days or 365 days for auditing? Legal/Compliance input needed — Aisha to loop GDPR/compliance and get recommendation by 2026-03-20.

Action items (owners + target dates)
- Marco: Create serving-runtime telemetry envelope PR with schema & example logs. Target: 2026-03-17. Linked: PR draft (see linked_artifacts).
- Jing: Prototype micro-eval harness + instructions for teams to add prompt-sets, run locally. Target: 2026-03-24.
- Samir & Oliver: Draft minimal telemetry contract for Private deploys (fields + retention + encryption). Target: 2026-03-17.
- Lena: Update release playbook to include two-stage promotion and rollback playbook including incident templates. Target: 2026-03-19.
- Aisha: Draft RFC update capturing agreed decisions and add optional config knobs for Dedicated customers; send to product/security for sign-off. Target: 2026-03-16.
- Platform Eng (team): Prototype pipeline in a sandbox using a real lightweight model (tiny-lm) to exercise signature verification + canary gating. Target: alpha by 2026-04-02.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: False positives in quality gating (semantic changes flagged as regressions). Mitigation: allow manual hold and fast rollback; add human review path for low-confidence flags.
- Risk: Telemetry gaps in Private deployments -> blind rollouts. Mitigation: minimal telemetry contract + customer onboarding checklist; fallback: require manual promotion for no-telemetry customers.
- Risk: Increased token cost from new model variants. Mitigation: token-cost gating and finance alerting for >10% cost delta.

Notes from discussion (raw)
- Jing: "We need to be clear about what the eval snapshot captures — both model outputs and the exact prompt/preproc pipeline."
- Marco: "Serving runtime will need a versioned contract for latency buckets; we'll include coarse buckets initially (<=50ms, <=100ms, <=250ms, <=500ms, >500ms)."
- Samir: "For HSM-backed signatures, we should support both Redwood-managed KMS and BYO HSM certificates for on-prem customers."

Next meeting / checkpoints
- Quick sync planned 2026-03-17 to review telemetry contract draft and serving-runtime PR.
- RFC update sent 2026-03-16; request 48-hour review window from product and security.

Appendix / useful links
- Baseline metric dashboards: platform -> model-deploy -> baseline-overview (link internal)
- Initial eval prompt set template: gitlab:/mlops/eval-templates/standard-promptset-v1
- Prototype artifact manifest schema (WIP): CONFLUENCE-MLPIPE-8172

End notes
This document is intended as the working decision journal for the MLOps integration push. It captures outcomes and the immediate engineering tasks necessary to move from RFC to prototype. If your team has objections or alternative proposals, please comment inline on this doc or add to JIRA-PLAT-1123."
